# ES Obsidian Hub runtime

Version **1.4.1** fixes overlapping Calendar date badges and meeting markers with separate rows and internally scrollable short calendars. Version **1.4.0** adds a shared widget frame, grouped lists and a Refresh all widgets action and visible-view automatic reads (YouTrack 6h, Calendar/Mail 10m, Slack 5m). Hide/Show widgets moves into Customize. Version 1.3.0 added optional Type icon preferences, built-in action/widget icons and restrained priority colors. Version 1.2.0 selectively ported compact cards, temporary search/Type filters and a read-only note preview from local runtime 0.28.0. Version 1.1.0 added Calendar / Mail from local runtime 0.27.0. This public fork began at 0.25.1 and keeps its configurable account setup. The historical plugin ID remains `aimultiple-kanban-extras`. The displayed name is ES Obsidian Hub.

Read the repository [README](../../../README.md), [AGENTS](../../../AGENTS.md) and [connection guide](../../../docs/CONNECTIONS.md). No personal notes, snapshots, tokens, local settings, global tool configuration or source-vault history is part of this package.

`main.js`, `manifest.json`, `styles.css` run directly in Obsidian. YouTrack uses `scripts/refresh-youtrack.py` and Python 3.11+. Calendar and Slack use Obsidian's runtime with no installed Node/Python dependencies. Mail requires the bundled `scripts/read-mail.applescript` and macOS `/usr/bin/osascript`. It uses no Python or additional installation. Keep the bundled ICAL license and source.

Each user connects YouTrack through local Keychain credentials and can opt into State sync with configurable state names. Imported notes retain their account identity. Slack's notes channel and user group are optional. The starter includes generic folders and recovers the board view after the initial plugin trust step. See [verification](../../../docs/VERIFICATION.md) for actual test scope.

The source below `// BEGIN LOCAL CALENDAR BUNDLE` is generated. Edit calendar adapter modules then run `node scripts/bundle-calendar.cjs` here. Keep other helpers above the marker.

The managed main board adds one filter row and compact Priority/Type buttons per card. Optional excerpts use the first nonempty text under Next step or Sonraki adım. Search matches rendered titles, paths, issue IDs and effective Types, with diacritic-insensitive matching; it combines with the Type selector. Filters stay in the rendered leaf and reset on reload. Column/WIP totals still describe the saved Base result.

**Customize → Type icons** discovers live Type folders and saves explicit choices from twelve built-in Lucide icons. No folder-name mapping ships in the defaults. Unconfigured or invalid entries use `folder`; renaming a folder does not migrate its preference. Choices decorate card Type chips and the Type picker, retaining text. `typeIcons` writes share the existing settings queue, preserve unrelated fields, reject stale folders/external conflicts and update the display only after a successful save. Rendering and startup do not save preferences or modify notes. No SVG packs, remote assets or third-party icon plugins are needed.

High/Urgent use theme-derived accents and distinct priority symbols; Medium/Low and Types stay neutral. Selection uses the theme accent. Done titles remain struck through, but managed card controls retain full opacity. Styles are scoped to Hub controls; vendor/theme files are unchanged.

Preview is a nonmodal, text-only Markdown subset: no YAML, HTML execution, embeds, remote images or plugin postprocessors. It reads at most a 2 MiB note and shows at most 50,000 characters; Open note opens or reuses a Markdown tab while preserving the board. Excerpts are bounded and cached in memory. Metadata/file events invalidate them, and redraw/unload cleans owned controls, listeners and panels. Card Priority/Type controls reuse existing guarded property actions; choosing Type can still move the note.

Generate the synthetic DOM check with `python3 -B tests/board.preview.py` from this folder. Serve its printed directory over localhost and open it in a browser. Use `?narrow=1&light=1&settings=1` or `?compact=1&preview=1` for panel variants. `?neutral=1` is a fixture-only comparison without priority accents. It measures sampled text/icon contrast, including an ancestor-opacity guard. The fixture uses fictional notes and mocked APIs; its placeholder SVG does not prove Lucide glyph availability. Check actual icons in native Obsidian. See the repository's [handoff](../../../docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#next-steps) and [verification record](../../../docs/VERIFICATION.md).

The shared refresh fans out to connected sources, including inactive Calendar/Mail tabs, without opening setup dialogs. It waits for all reads, isolates failures, retains previous results and respects adapter guards. Automatic YouTrack reads only update the snapshot, never imports or State. Its fresh persisted timestamp and in-session failure backoff defer retries; connection changes reset the interval. Calendar/YouTrack eligibility is checked on the existing one-minute Home tick. Mail schedules from completion and preserves permission-denial suppression. Unload cancels owned timers/processes.

All widgets follow the [design contract](../../../docs/DESIGN.md): 36 px header, 40 px controls, flexible body and 52 px footer. Mail/Slack date groups use local calendar days and preserve filtering, row limits and source actions. YouTrack groups by actual State while preserving per-issue identity and within-group order. Source errors remain inside the body; long context cannot wrap the frame. The standalone [HTML preview](../../../docs/prototypes/widget-lists.html) uses fictional data and also illustrates optional density/Agenda treatments. It is not a Notebook Navigator integration.
